title: The Insane Story Behind the Mid-Engine Corvette
description:
For sixty-six years, every Chevrolet Corvette had its engine in the front. Then, in July twenty nineteen, Chevrolet moved it behind the driver. It looked like a sudden revolution. It was not. The mid-engine Corvette was a dream that started in the nineteen fifties, survived secret prototypes, a rotary engine, an oil crisis, and the death of the man who wanted it most. That man was Zora Arkus-Duntov, the engineer often called the father of the Corvette. He spent decades pushing for a mid-engine car, and he was told no again and again. When he reviewed a new front-engined Corvette in the nineteen nineties, he reportedly summed up his frustration in one short sentence. The engine is still in the front.

Every figure in this video comes from a published source, listed below.
